stem: Which equation shows the total number of kits handed out?
stimulus: A health fair hands out $x$ adult first-aid kits that cost 4 dollars each and $y$ child first-aid kits that cost 3 dollars each. It hands out 60 kits in all, at a total cost of 210 dollars.
explanation: The question asks how many kits there are, so you only count them: $x$ adult kits plus $y$ child kits make 60 kits. The prices don't belong in this equation. This is the 'count' equation, the first half of every question where you pick the system that matches a story.

A.why: You added the kits correctly but set them equal to the money total. 210 is dollars, not kits, so it belongs in the cost equation.

C.why: You put the prices on the variables but kept the kit total of 60. Once a price multiplies a count, the result is dollars, so the total would have to be 210.

D.why: You added the two prices to get 7 and applied it to every kit. Each kit has its own price, so the cost equation would be $4x + 3y$, and the count equation has no prices at all.

stem: Which equation shows the total number of hours spent drawing maps?
stimulus: A mapmaker draws $x$ trail maps, which take 3 hours each, and $y$ city maps, which take 5 hours each. Drawing all the maps takes 47 hours in total.
explanation: Each trail map takes 3 hours, so $x$ trail maps take $3x$ hours. Each city map takes 5 hours, so $y$ city maps take $5y$ hours. Together that is 47 hours. This is the 'value' equation (rate times quantity for each type) that you need when you pick the system that matches a story.

A.why: This counts maps, but 47 is a number of hours. A count equation needs a count total, and this story doesn't give one.

B.why: You swapped the rates and gave trail maps 5 hours and city maps 3 hours. Check which number goes with which variable: $x$ is trail maps, which take 3 hours each.

D.why: You divided by the hours per map when you should have multiplied. If each map takes 3 hours, then $x$ maps take $3x$ hours, not $\frac{x}{3}$.

stimulus: A factory employs $x$ part-time workers and $y$ full-time workers. The factory has 3 times as many full-time workers as part-time workers.
explanation: There are more full-time workers, so $y$ is the larger number. To get it, you multiply the part-time count by 3: $y = 3x$. As a check, 10 part-time workers would mean 30 full-time workers. Many 'pick the system' questions use a 'times as many' sentence in place of a count equation.

B.why: You put the 3 on the wrong group. $x = 3y$ says there are 3 times as many part-time workers. Test it: if $y = 10$, then $x = 30$, which is the reverse of the story.

C.why: You turned 'times as many' into 'more than'. $y = x + 3$ means 3 more full-time workers, not 3 times as many.

D.why: You treated 3 as the total number of workers. The 3 compares the two groups. It isn't a headcount.

stem: Which expression gives the cost, in dollars, of the $x$ kits after the discount?
stimulus: An immunology lab buys $x$ antibody test kits. Each kit has a list price of 50 dollars, and the lab gets 20% off every kit.
explanation: With 20% off, the lab pays 80% of the price. Multiply by 0.8: $0.8(50x) = 40x$, which is 40 dollars per kit. This is the discounted 'value' term that appears in 'pick the system' questions about sales and coupons.

A.why: You subtracted the percent from the price. Taking 0.2 off 50 dollars leaves 49.80 dollars, which is a 20-cent discount, not 20%. Multiply by what is left, 0.8, instead.

B.why: You multiplied by the 20% that is taken off, so this is the amount saved. The lab pays the other 80%.

C.why: You read 20% off as 20 dollars off. 20% of 50 dollars is 10 dollars, so each kit costs 40 dollars, not 30.
